name: Shimei son of Gera
charge: Cursing the king and casting stones at him: come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial
summary: As David reached Bahurim on the road out of Jerusalem, a man of Saul’s family came out cursing him all the way, throwing stones and dust, and saying the Lord had paid him back for all the blood of Saul’s house. Saul was the wicked one who had tried to kill David, and it was the hand of the Most High that stopped him, yet Shimei cursed the king as though David were in the wrong. David would not let Abishai take his head, but said to let him curse, because the Lord had told him to. He swore Shimei would not die, and left the case to Solomon.
offenseFull: When David reached Bahurim, Shimei the son of Gera, of the family of Saul’s house, came out cursing him all the way and throwing stones at David and his servants, though the people and the mighty men surrounded the king. He called David a man of blood and a man of Belial and told him to get out; the Lord, he said, had paid him back for all the blood of Saul’s house, whose throne he had taken, and had handed the kingdom to his son Absalom, and he was caught in his own evil because he was a man of blood (2 Samuel 16:5-13; 2 Samuel 16:5-8). Saul was the wicked one who tried to kill David, and it was by the hand of the Most High that Saul did not succeed; yet Shimei cursed him as though David were the one in the wrong, because word gets around, people gossip and blame, and he saw the king in a low state and went to rub it in his face. He truly thought he was right in it. The law forbids reviling the gods or cursing the ruler of the people (Exodus 22:28), and the gods there are the leaders set over the people, for the Most High called the judges gods and children of the Most High (Psalms 82:6). Paul obeyed that very verse when he was checked for

Abishai the son of Zeruiah asked why this dead dog should curse the king, and asked leave to go over and take off his head. The king asked what he had to do with them, the sons of Zeruiah: if the Lord had told Shimei to curse David, who could question him? If his own son was seeking his life, how much more this Benjamite. He told them to leave him alone and let him curse, for the Lord had told him to, and perhaps the Lord would look on his affliction and repay him with good for that day’s cursing (2 Samuel 16:9-13). David rolled with mighty men of war and Abishai was ready to take the man’s head off his shoulders, but if it was of the Most High, then let it come; the same as when people come into our forums to bicker and bring confusion, sometimes to try the patience of men who prayed for patience. So David went on his way while Shimei kept pace along the hillside, cursing, throwing stones and flinging dust (2 Samuel 16:13). To endure suffering patiently after doing well is what pleases God (1 Peter 2:20).
judgmentFull: When the king came back over the Jordan, Shimei hurried down with a thousand men of Benjamin, fell before him, and begged him not to hold against him the wrong he had done the day the king left Jerusalem, for he knew he had sinned. Abishai said he should die for cursing the Lord’s anointed; David again rebuked the sons of Zeruiah and asked whether anyone should be put to death in Israel the day he was king again. So he swore to Shimei that he would not die (2 Samuel 19:18-23; 2 Samuel 19:16-23). David understood grace long before the New Testament; grace has always been around. Mercy gave the man his life; it did not make the curse true. At the last David charged Solomon concerning Shimei, who had cursed him bitterly on the day he went to Mahanaim and then met him at the Jordan, where David swore by the Lord not to kill him; Solomon was not to count him innocent, but as a wise man he would know what to do (1 Kings 2:8-9). Solomon had him build a house in Jerusalem and stay there, warning him that on the day he crossed the brook Kidron he would die and the blame would be his own; Shimei called the terms good and agreed (1 Kings 2:36-46; 1 Kings 2:36-38). Three years later he rode to Achish king of Gath after two servants who had run off, and brought them back (1 Kings 2:39-40). Solomon asked why he had not kept the oath of the Lord and the command he had called good, told him he knew all the wickedness he had done to David, and said the Lord would bring it back on him (1 Kings 2:42-44). Benaiah the son of Jehoiada struck him down, and Solomon’s kingdom was made secure (1 Kings 2:46). He had been given a condition for his life and had agreed to it, and two runaway servants proved more urgent to him than the word his safety stood on; the pardon of the father did not entitle him to break the charge of the son.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not curse or speak evil of civil rulers or dignitaries.
It is not proper to despise government.
You are to keep your word.
Libel and name calling is condemned by Christ.

text.text: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:

The Lord hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the Lord hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou art taken in thy mischief, because thou art a bloody man.
Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the Lord hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the Lord hath bidden him.
It may be that the Lord will look on mine affliction, and that the Lord will requite me good for his cursing this day.

For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the Lord’s anointed?

And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?
Therefore the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.
And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.

Therefore the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.

And, behold, thou hast with thee Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite of Bahurim, which cursed me with a grievous curse in the day when I went to Mahanaim: but he came down to meet me at Jordan, and I sware to him by the Lord, saying, I will not put thee to death with the sword.
Now therefore hold him not guiltless: for thou art a wise man, and knowest what thou oughtest to do unto him; but his hoar head bring thou down to the grave with blood.
And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Build thee an house in Jerusalem, and dwell there, and go not forth thence any whither.
For it shall be, that on the day thou goest out, and passest over the brook Kidron, thou shalt know for certain that thou shalt surely die: thy blood shall be upon thine own head.
And Shimei said unto the king, The saying is good: as my lord the king hath said, so will thy servant do. And Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.
And it came to pass at the end of three years, that two of the servants of Shimei ran away unto Achish son of Maachah king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, Behold, thy servants be in Gath.
And Shimei arose, and saddled his ass, and went to Gath to Achish to seek his servants: and Shimei went, and brought his servants from Gath.
And it was told Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath, and was come again.

And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Did I not make thee to swear by the Lord, and protested unto thee, saying, Know for a certain, on the day thou goest out, and walkest abroad any whither, that thou shalt surely die? and thou saidst unto me, The word that I have heard is good.
Why then hast thou not kept the oath of the Lord, and the commandment that I have charged thee with?

The king said moreover to Shimei, Thou knowest all the wickedness which thine heart is privy to, that thou didst to David my father: therefore the Lord shall return thy wickedness upon thine own head;
